item.content:encoded:
Team4Tech is inviting education-focused nonprofits and NGOs operating in Africa to apply for its Experience AI Cohort, a free, structured learning programme designed to help nonprofit staff and teachers build practical knowledge and confidence in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Developed by the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Google DeepMind, Experience AI provides research-based educational resources for teachers and students aged 11–14. Through the three-month cohort, selected organizations will participate in live virtual sessions, self-paced learning, coaching, and peer-learning activities to develop the skills needed to introduce AI literacy to their learning communities.

About the Experience AI Cohort

The programme will run from September through early December 2026 and will support participating NGOs in understanding the foundations of AI and implementing Experience AI lessons with teachers and learners.

Participants will explore how AI is used in everyday life, how computers learn from data, and how issues such as limited datasets can contribute to bias. They will also gain practical experience training and testing machine learning models and learn strategies for identifying misinformation in an increasingly AI-driven world.

The programme will also introduce participants to AI-related career pathways, helping educators prepare young people for a future where AI and digital skills are increasingly important.

What Participants Will Learn

Through the Experience AI programme, participants will:

  • Explore how artificial intelligence is used in the world today.
  • Understand how computers learn from data using machine learning.
  • Discover how limited datasets can contribute to bias.
  • Train and test a machine learning model to address a real-world problem.
  • Develop strategies for distinguishing facts from false information in the age of AI.
  • Learn about careers and opportunities related to artificial intelligence.
  • Build confidence in delivering practical AI learning experiences.

What Participating NGOs Will Receive

Selected organizations will have access to:

  • Research-based Experience AI resources and coursework.
  • Live virtual learning and peer-learning sessions.
  • Self-paced learning modules.
  • Coaching and facilitation from Team4Tech.
  • Opportunities to strengthen staff knowledge and practical AI skills.
  • An implementation stipend upon successful completion of the required course activities.

The stipend can be used to support the organization’s implementation of the learning and strategies developed through the cohort.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for education nonprofits and NGOs operating in Africa that are interested in using Experience AI lessons to strengthen AI literacy among teachers and learners.

Participating organizations are expected to nominate 2–4 staff members who can commit approximately 15–20 total hours over three months.

Organizations should also be prepared to:

  • Complete asynchronous learning activities and assignments.
  • Attend six live virtual sessions focused on peer learning, sharing, and feedback.
  • Complete pre- and post-cohort surveys.
  • Complete a follow-up survey approximately 4–6 months after participation.
  • Develop plans for implementing Experience AI within their organization and learner community.

Participants should also be comfortable completing coursework and participating in coaching sessions in English.

Who Will Benefit?

The programme is particularly relevant to organizations working with teachers and young learners aged 11–14.

By participating, NGOs can build their internal capacity to introduce young people to foundational AI concepts, responsible use of technology, machine learning, bias, misinformation, and AI-related careers.

Organizations will also have the opportunity to share their learning with additional staff and teachers. Applicants are asked to indicate how many additional educators they expect to train on Experience AI lessons within the following 6–12 months.

Expected Impact

Experience AI can help participating organizations strengthen their education programmes by giving educators practical tools and knowledge to introduce AI concepts in an accessible way.

Through the cohort, participating NGOs can develop strategies for integrating AI literacy into their existing programmes, help teachers become more confident in discussing AI with students, and give learners opportunities to understand how AI systems work rather than simply using AI tools.

The programme can therefore contribute to stronger digital skills, AI awareness, critical thinking, and career readiness among young people.

Important Dates

Application Deadline: September 4, 2026

Selection Decisions: September 16–18, 2026

Programme Period: September 2026 – early December 2026

Up to 10 NGOs operating in Africa are expected to participate in the cohort.

How to Apply

Interested NGOs should complete the Experience AI Cohort application form before the September 4, 2026 deadline.

Application: Apply for the Experience AI Cohort

For questions specifically about the Experience AI cohort, applicants can contact Michelle Mwangi at michelle@team4tech.org. For other questions, contact community@team4tech.org.

Conclusion

The Team4Tech Experience AI Cohort 2026 provides African education nonprofits with an opportunity to strengthen their staff capacity in artificial intelligence and bring practical AI learning experiences to teachers and young people.

With free coursework, live sessions, coaching, research-based resources, and an implementation stipend, the programme can help participating organizations take meaningful steps toward building AI-ready learning communities.

item.content:encoded:
The Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program offers an opportunity for ambitious university students to gain practical experience in financial services while developing their knowledge of credit, risk management, banking, and business operations.

The internship is part of Truist’s broad-based early-career internship programme, which combines education, professional exposure, and practical work experience. Through the Credit track, interns are connected with lines of business within Wholesale Banking, giving them an opportunity to develop an understanding of the day-to-day responsibilities involved in areas such as Commercial & Corporate Banking, Specialized Industries and Wholesale Payments.

The programme is designed for students who are interested in building careers in financial services and who want to complement their university education with hands-on experience in a major banking environment.

The position was posted on August 18, 2026, and is listed as available in five locations across the Truist footprint. The supplied job announcement does not specify a closing date, meaning interested candidates should not wait for a deadline before submitting an application.

About the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program

The Credit Internship Program is a temporary internship opportunity designed to develop early-career talent for roles connected to Truist’s Wholesale Banking business.

Rather than focusing exclusively on classroom learning, the programme combines structured training with practical assignments and exposure to real business activities.

Interns can expect to participate in:

  • Educational and professional development sessions.
  • Business rotations.
  • Special projects and assignments.
  • Day-to-day business activities.
  • Training related to credit and risk.
  • Team-based projects.
  • Activities involving internal business partners and external clients.
  • Exposure to senior leaders and, potentially, executive leaders.

This combination is intended to help interns understand how financial institutions operate while strengthening the technical, analytical, communication, and leadership capabilities required for a career in financial services.

What Is the Credit Track?

The Credit track is specifically aligned with business lines within Wholesale Banking.

Interns may gain exposure to areas such as:

Commercial and Corporate Banking

This area involves supporting businesses and corporate clients with financial services and banking solutions. Interns can gain insight into how financial institutions evaluate business needs, manage relationships, and assess financial and credit considerations.

Specialized Industries

This area focuses on specific industry sectors and their unique financial requirements. Exposure to specialized industries can help interns understand how economic conditions, industry dynamics, and business models influence financial decision-making.

Wholesale Payments

Wholesale Payments focuses on financial solutions and payment services for business and institutional clients. Exposure to this area can help interns understand the role of financial infrastructure and payment systems in supporting businesses.

The specific business area assigned to an intern will depend on the host team and programme placement.

What Can Interns Expect During the Program?

Truist describes the programme as one that combines education, exposure, and experience.

This means successful interns are not simply expected to observe employees. They will have opportunities to participate in work that supports internal business partners and external clients while applying concepts learned during training.

Interns will also be expected to work collaboratively and contribute to projects and activities assigned by their rotational leads.

The programme is therefore suitable for students who want to gain practical experience while developing a deeper understanding of financial services.

Exposure to Truist Senior Leaders

One notable feature of the programme is exposure to Truist senior leadership.

The internship may include sessions involving senior leaders and executive leaders, giving participants an opportunity to learn about the organization, its business operations, and the expectations associated with careers in financial services.

For students preparing for careers in banking, finance, credit, or related areas, this type of professional exposure can provide useful insight into the financial-services industry and corporate leadership.

Key Responsibilities of a Credit Intern

Successful interns will be expected to undertake a range of responsibilities throughout the programme.

1. Learn Credit and Risk Management Concepts

Interns will learn a broad range of concepts related to risk management, enterprise programmes and financial services.

This training is intended to prepare them for assignments within different lines of business.

2. Develop Analytical and Decision-Making Skills

Credit and financial-services careers require employees to evaluate information, identify risks, and make informed decisions.

The programme therefore emphasizes the development of analytical and decision-making capabilities.

Interns will have opportunities to apply these skills through practical projects and business assignments.

3. Strengthen Communication Skills

Effective communication is an important requirement of the internship.

Interns may work with internal business partners, external clients, managers, and other members of their teams. They will therefore need to communicate information clearly and professionally.

4. Develop Leadership Skills

The programme also seeks to strengthen leadership capabilities.

Students can develop leadership skills through project participation, teamwork, initiative, campus involvement, and other professional responsibilities.

5. Complete Special Projects

Interns may be assigned special projects or other tasks outside the formal training programme.

These assignments can provide opportunities to demonstrate initiative, analytical thinking, organization and problem-solving skills.

6. Participate in Business Rotations

Business rotations form an important part of the programme.

Through rotations, interns can work on projects and participate in normal business activities, allowing them to apply concepts and behaviours learned during training.

7. Complete Additional Training

Managers may recommend additional training during or after the internship programme.

This can help interns continue developing relevant skills and knowledge based on their assignments and career interests.

Academic Requirements

The Truist Credit Internship Program is intended for students who are actively pursuing a university degree.

Applicants must be working toward either:

  • A Bachelor’s degree; or
  • A Master’s degree.

Truist particularly values candidates studying business-related disciplines, with accounting and finance coursework preferred.

A 3.0 or higher GPA is preferred.

The GPA requirement is described as preferred rather than an absolute minimum, meaning candidates should carefully review the complete application requirements rather than assuming that applicants below 3.0 are automatically excluded.

Graduation Requirement

Another important requirement concerns the expected graduation date.

Applicants should have a scheduled final-degree graduation date between the following:

December 2027 and June 2029.

Students outside this graduation window may therefore not fit the target profile for this particular internship programme.

Prospective applicants should carefully compare their expected graduation date with the requirement before applying.

Skills Truist Is Looking For

The programme is designed for students who can demonstrate a combination of academic preparation, interpersonal abilities, and professional potential.

Important skills and qualities include:

Strong Communication

Candidates should possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

This is important because interns may work with multiple stakeholders, participate in meetings, collaborate on projects, and potentially interact with clients.

Initiative

Truist seeks students who demonstrate strong initiative.

Applicants should be able to show situations where they have taken responsibility, identified opportunities, solved problems, or gone beyond basic expectations.

Leadership

Demonstrated leadership is another important requirement.

Leadership may be demonstrated through:

  • Campus organizations.
  • Student leadership positions.
  • Volunteer activities.
  • Work experience.
  • Academic projects.
  • Community initiatives.
  • Team activities.
  • Other situations where the applicant has taken responsibility and influenced positive outcomes.

Analytical Ability

Because the Credit track is associated with credit and risk, analytical thinking is highly relevant.

Students should be comfortable working with information, evaluating situations, and drawing logical conclusions.

Financial Services Interest

Candidates should have genuine enthusiasm for pursuing a career in financial services.

A demonstrated interest in banking, finance, credit, accounting, risk management, or related fields can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Technical Skills Required

Applicants should be proficient in:

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint

Excel is particularly useful in financial-services environments where employees may work with financial information, calculations, analysis, and reporting.

PowerPoint can be useful for presentations, project updates, business proposals, and communicating analytical findings.

Students should therefore ensure that they can confidently use both programmes before entering the internship.

Financial Services Knowledge

Truist also seeks candidates with general knowledge of the financial services industry.

Students should therefore understand fundamental concepts related to banking, finance, credit, and risk.

Applicants do not necessarily need extensive professional experience because the programme is designed for early-career talent. However, demonstrating an informed interest in financial services can help distinguish a candidate.

Relocation Requirement

The internship is not necessarily conducted in one fixed location.

Truist states that individuals hired into the programme will relocate throughout the Truist footprint based on their assigned host team.

The specific location will be included in the internship offer letter.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to relocate if required.

This is an important consideration for students who currently live outside the assigned internship location.

Travel Requirement

Candidates must also demonstrate a willingness to travel for on-the-job training.

Students considering this opportunity should therefore be comfortable with travel and potential changes in work location associated with training and programme activities.

Hybrid Learning and Training

Training sessions throughout the summer may use a hybrid approach, combining remote and in-person learning.

This provides flexibility while still allowing interns to participate in face-to-face professional development and workplace experiences.

The precise balance between remote and in-person activities may depend on the programme and assigned team.

Employment Authorization Requirement

One of the most important eligibility considerations is Truist’s employment-authorization policy.

The company explicitly states that it will not sponsor applicants for employment authorization for this position.

The company also states that it will not provide immigration-related support for several categories of immigration status, including:

  • H-1B;
  • F-1 OPT;
  • F-1 STEM OPT;
  • F-1 CPT;
  • J-1;
  • TN-1;
  • TN-2;
  • E-3; and
  • Sponsorship for U.S. permanent residence.

Applicants should therefore carefully assess their existing U.S. employment authorization before applying.

This requirement is particularly important for international students studying in the United States who may normally rely on post-study or student-related employment authorization.

English Language Requirement

The job posting identifies English as required.

Candidates should therefore have sufficient English-language proficiency to communicate effectively in a professional banking environment.

This includes the ability to participate in meetings, communicate with colleagues, prepare professional documents and presentations, and interact appropriately with internal and external stakeholders.

Internship Employment Type

The position is classified as temporary.

This is consistent with its structure as an internship programme designed to provide students with professional experience before completion of their degree.

Students should therefore distinguish the programme from a permanent full-time position.

Internship Locations

The job posting states that the Credit Internship Program is available in five locations.

The specific location for an individual intern will depend on the assigned host team and will be communicated in the offer letter.

Because relocation is part of the programme expectations, applicants should be prepared to work at the location assigned to them.

Compensation Information

For work locations in Washington, D.C., the posting states an annualized hourly wage of:

$25.00 per hour.

The posting provides this figure specifically to comply with Washington, D.C. pay transparency requirements.

Applicants should note that the stated rate applies to Washington, D.C. work locations and should not automatically be assumed to apply to every location where the internship is available.

Benefits Information

The job posting includes a general description of benefits available to eligible Truist employees.

However, it specifically explains that regular employees working 20 hours or more per week may be eligible for benefits, while temporary or contingent workers may not qualify for the same benefits.

The posting therefore advises applicants to review the specific benefits applicable to their employment status and position.

General Truist benefits described in the posting include the following:

  • Medical coverage.
  • Dental coverage.
  • Vision coverage.
  • Life insurance.
  • Disability coverage.
  • Accidental death and dismemberment coverage.
  • Tax-preferred savings accounts.
  • 401(k) plan.
  • Vacation.
  • Sick days.
  • Paid holidays.

Eligibility for specific benefits depends on employment classification, division, hours worked, and other applicable conditions.

Truist’s Purpose and Values

Truist states that its purpose is to inspire and build better lives and communities.

The company emphasizes caring for clients, empowering teammates, and serving communities.

The organization provides services across areas including:

  • Consumer banking.
  • Wholesale banking.
  • Technology.
  • Data.
  • Operations.

Interns are expected to embrace and model Truist’s purpose, mission, and values during the programme.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Truist states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The company says it does not discriminate based on characteristics including:

  • Race.
  • Gender.
  • Color.
  • Religion.
  • Citizenship.
  • National origin.
  • Age.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Gender identity.
  • Disability.
  • Veteran status.
  • Other classifications protected by law.

The opportunity, therefore, does not specify a particular race, ethnicity, or continent as a prerequisite.

However, the employment-authorization requirement remains an important condition for applicants.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suitable for students who are:

  • Studying finance, accounting, business, or a related field.
  • Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree.
  • Expected to graduate between December 2027 and June 2029.
  • Interested in banking and financial services.
  • Interested in credit and risk management.
  • Comfortable working with Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong communicators.
  • Analytical and detail-oriented.
  • Demonstrated leaders.
  • Proactive and willing to take initiative.
  • Comfortable working collaboratively.
  • Willing to travel.
  • Willing to relocate.
  • Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship.

How Applicants Can Prepare a Strong Application

Students interested in the Truist Credit Internship Program should approach the application strategically.

1. Review Your Graduation Date

Confirm that your expected final-degree graduation date falls between December 2027 and June 2029.

2. Highlight Relevant Coursework

If you are studying business, accounting, finance, or another related field, make sure relevant coursework is clearly reflected in your application.

Courses related to financial analysis, accounting, economics, corporate finance, banking, risk management, or related areas can demonstrate alignment with the Credit track.

3. Demonstrate Leadership

Do not simply state that you have leadership skills.

Provide examples of how you have demonstrated leadership through campus organizations, employment, academic projects, community initiatives, or other activities.

4. Emphasize Analytical Skills

Highlight academic, professional, or extracurricular experiences that required research, analysis, problem-solving, or decision-making.

5. Demonstrate Financial Services Interest

Explain why you are interested in banking, credit, risk, or financial services and how the internship fits into your longer-term career objectives.

6. Strengthen Your Excel and PowerPoint Skills

Because Excel and PowerPoint proficiency is specifically listed among the requirements, applicants should ensure that these skills are clearly represented in their resumes and applications where appropriate.

7. Prepare for Relocation

Applicants should be comfortable with the possibility of relocating within the Truist footprint.

8. Confirm Employment Authorization

This is particularly important for international students and other candidates who may require immigration support.

Truist explicitly states that it will not sponsor employment authorization for this internship, so applicants should confirm that they independently meet the employment-authorization requirement before applying.

Key Facts About the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program

Feature Details
Opportunity 2027 Credit Internship Program
Organization Truist
Category Internship
Employment type Temporary
Sector Banking and financial services
Track Credit
Business area Wholesale Banking
Degree level Bachelor’s or Master’s
Preferred fields Business, accounting and finance
Preferred GPA 3.0+
Graduation window December 2027 to June 2029
Language English required
Technical skills Excel and PowerPoint
Locations Five U.S. locations
Relocation Required based on assigned host team
Travel Required for on-the-job training
U.S. work authorization Required; no sponsorship
Washington, D.C. stated wage $25 per hour
Posted August 18, 2026
Application deadline Not specified in the provided posting

Is There an Application Deadline?

The supplied Truist job announcement does not provide a specific application closing date.

Because internship recruitment can be competitive and positions can close when hiring needs are met, students who meet the requirements should consider applying as soon as possible rather than waiting for a deadline to be announced.

The posting was published on August 18, 2026.

Application Process

Candidates interested in the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program should use the official Truist careers platform to review the position and submit an application.

The job posting explains that applicants should click the Apply Now button and complete the application.

After completing the application, candidates will be invited to create a profile that allows them to:

  • Track their application status.
  • Receive communications relating to their application.
  • Access relevant recruitment information.

Candidates who already have a Truist profile can log in to review their application status.

APPLY HERE

Application Accommodation

Truist states that candidates with disabilities who require assistance during the application process may request a reasonable accommodation.

The recruitment information provides a dedicated accessibility contact for accommodation requests.

Applicants requiring an accommodation should use the official contact information provided in the Truist job announcement rather than sending unrelated recruitment inquiries through the accommodation channel.

Why This Internship Could Be Valuable for Students

The Credit Internship Program is structured around three central components: education, exposure, and experience.

Students receive structured learning while gaining exposure to professionals and senior leaders and participating in practical business activities.

The Credit track can be particularly relevant for students considering careers in:

  • Commercial banking.
  • Corporate banking.
  • Credit analysis.
  • Risk management.
  • Wholesale banking.
  • Financial services.
  • Financial analysis.
  • Banking operations.
  • Specialized industry banking.
  • Wholesale payments.

The experience can help students understand how financial concepts are applied in a professional environment while developing transferable skills in communication, analysis, leadership, and teamwork.

Visit HERE for more information about the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program.

Conclusion

The Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program is a strong early-career opportunity for students pursuing degrees in business, finance, accounting, and related disciplines who want to gain practical experience in the financial services industry.

The programme combines structured education with professional exposure, business rotations, special projects, and practical assignments. Interns can develop their understanding of credit, risk management, and wholesale banking while strengthening analytical, communication, and leadership skills.

The programme is particularly suited to students graduating between December 2027 and June 2029, with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher and an interest in financial services. Applicants should also be proficient in Excel and PowerPoint, demonstrate leadership and initiative, and be willing to travel and relocate according to their assigned host team.

A critical consideration for applicants is U.S. employment authorization. Truist explicitly states that it will not provide employment sponsorship or immigration-related support for this position. Candidates should therefore verify their eligibility to work in the United States before submitting an application.

The posting was published on August 18, 2026, and no specific application deadline is stated in the provided announcement. Given the competitive nature of internship recruitment, eligible students should review the official posting and submit their applications as early as possible.

For students seeking to turn their academic knowledge into practical experience in credit, banking, and financial services, the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program provides an opportunity to learn, contribute, and build a foundation for a future career in the financial sector.

For more global Internship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship 2027 presents an exceptional opportunity for outstanding international students seeking to pursue an undergraduate degree in Canada. Recognized as the University of Toronto’s most prestigious scholarship for international students, the programme is designed to support exceptional young people who demonstrate outstanding academic achievement, creativity, leadership potential, and the ability to make a positive contribution to the global community.

The highly competitive scholarship provides comprehensive financial support for four years of undergraduate study at the University of Toronto, covering tuition, books, incidental fees, and full residence support. Approximately 37 students are selected as Pearson Scholars each year, making this one of the most significant undergraduate scholarship opportunities available to international students in Canada.

For prospective students looking for a fully funded undergraduate scholarship in Canada, the Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship offers not only financial assistance but also the opportunity to join a diverse international community at one of Canada’s leading universities.

What Is the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship?

The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship is a prestigious University of Toronto scholarship created to recognize exceptional international students entering first-entry undergraduate programmes.

The scholarship focuses on students who have demonstrated more than academic excellence. The University of Toronto seeks candidates who have shown creativity, leadership potential, and a commitment to contributing positively to the global community.

Pearson Scholars become part of a global community of exceptional students and gain access to the University of Toronto’s academic environment, resources, and broader international student community.

The scholarship is particularly significant because it provides financial support for the full duration of an undergraduate programme, helping successful students overcome some of the major financial barriers associated with studying in Canada.

What Does the Pearson Scholarship Cover?

One of the most attractive features of the Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is its comprehensive financial coverage.

Successful scholars receive support covering:

  • Tuition fees for four years.
  • Books required during their studies.
  • Incidental fees associated with their university education.
  • Full residence support for four years.

The scholarship is tenable only at the University of Toronto and applies to first-entry undergraduate programmes.

This means applicants should understand that the scholarship is specifically designed for students entering undergraduate studies rather than students who are already enrolled in post-secondary education.

The University of Toronto describes the programme as one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada. The programme has previously attracted students from around the world, with the university reporting representation from 188 countries.

How Competitive Is the University of Toronto Pearson Scholarship?

The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is highly competitive.

Approximately 37 students are named Pearson Scholars each year, meaning applicants are selected from a very strong international pool of candidates.

The university’s selection criteria go beyond academic grades. Applicants are expected to demonstrate a combination of:

  1. Outstanding academic achievement.
  2. Creativity.
  3. Leadership potential.
  4. A demonstrated ability or potential to contribute positively to the global community.

Students therefore should not approach the scholarship application as simply an academic award. Their wider achievements, leadership experiences, creativity, personal qualities and potential impact are important components of the opportunity.

Who Is Eligible for the Pearson International Scholarship 2027?

To be considered for the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship 2027, applicants must satisfy the University of Toronto’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants must be international students, meaning they must be non-Canadian students who require a study permit to study in Canada.

They must also meet the relevant secondary-school requirements. For the 2027 scholarship, eligible students must be:

  • Enrolled in their final year of senior secondary school during the 2026–2027 academic year; or
  • Have graduated from secondary school no earlier than June 2026.

In addition, successful candidates must be prepared to begin their undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027.

Who Is Not Eligible?

The University of Toronto also identifies circumstances in which students cannot be considered for the Pearson Scholarship.

Students are not eligible if they are already attending post-secondary studies.

Students who begin their post-secondary studies in January 2027, whether at the University of Toronto or another post-secondary institution, are also not eligible.

The scholarship is therefore specifically targeted at students transitioning from secondary school into their first-entry undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto.

High School Nomination Is Mandatory

An important feature of the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship is that students cannot simply apply independently without a school nomination.

Applicants must first be nominated by their current secondary school.

Students should therefore speak with their

  • Guidance counsellor;
  • Principal;
  • Head of school; or
  • Another appropriate school official responsible for scholarship nominations.

Each eligible high school can nominate only one student per year.

This makes it important for prospective applicants to begin discussions with their schools well before the nomination deadline.

Students should explain their academic achievements, leadership experiences, extracurricular activities, community involvement, and other accomplishments to their school so that the school can make an informed decision about its nominee.

What If Your School Has Never Participated?

The University of Toronto allows schools that have not previously participated in the Pearson Scholarship programme to apply to join the programme.

Schools that have previously participated will receive access to the nomination form beginning July 6, 2026.

The deadline for schools to nominate a student is

October 9, 2026.

Schools that have not previously participated can apply to join the programme by noon Eastern Standard Time on October 9, 2026.

Students whose schools have not participated previously should therefore raise the opportunity with their school administration as early as possible.

University of Toronto Admission Application

Being nominated by a secondary school is only one part of the Pearson Scholarship process.

After nomination, the student must also apply for admission to the University of Toronto.

To be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply to at least one undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto and plan to begin their studies in September 2027.

The deadline to apply for admission to the University of Toronto and be considered for the Pearson Scholarship is:

October 16, 2026.

Applicants can apply to up to three areas of study on their University of Toronto admission application.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the university’s rules because, if they receive the Pearson Scholarship, the award will be restricted to their top choice of programme at the time scholarship decisions are made.

Pearson Scholarship Application Deadline

After being nominated by their school and submitting their University of Toronto admission application, eligible nominees will receive a private link to the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship application.

The scholarship application can be completed only after the student has submitted their University of Toronto admission application.

The final deadline to complete the Pearson Scholarship application and submit all required documentation is

November 6, 2026.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day. Because the process involves school nomination, university admission, and a separate scholarship application, prospective candidates should plan their applications several weeks or months in advance.

Key Pearson Scholarship 2027 Deadlines

The major dates prospective applicants should remember are:

  1. July 6, 2026 – Participating high schools receive access to the nomination form.
  2. October 9, 2026 – Deadline for high school nominations.
  3. October 9, 2026, by noon EST – Deadline for schools that have never participated to apply to join the programme.
  4. October 16, 2026 – Deadline for students to submit their University of Toronto admission application and be considered for the scholarship.
  5. November 6, 2026 – Final deadline for completing the Pearson Scholarship application and submitting the required documentation.
  6. September 2027 – Successful scholars begin their undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto.

What Makes a Strong Pearson Scholarship Candidate?

Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should understand that simply meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee selection.

The University of Toronto specifically identifies three major qualities among Pearson Scholars:

1. Academic Excellence

Applicants should have a strong academic record and demonstrate exceptional achievement during their secondary education.

Academic performance provides an important foundation for the scholarship because Pearson Scholars are expected to succeed in a demanding university environment.

2. Creativity

The scholarship also recognizes creativity.

This does not necessarily mean creativity only in artistic activities. Students can demonstrate creativity through innovation, problem-solving, entrepreneurship, research, technology, community projects, leadership initiatives or other activities where they have developed original approaches to challenges.

3. Leadership Potential

Leadership is another important consideration.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate situations in which they have taken initiative, influenced others, organized activities, solved problems, supported their communities or contributed meaningfully to their schools or wider society.

Leadership does not necessarily require holding a formal title. What matters is the impact and initiative demonstrated by the applicant.

Why International Students Should Consider This Opportunity

For international students seeking an undergraduate scholarship in Canada, the Pearson Scholarship stands out because of its extensive financial coverage.

Studying internationally can involve substantial costs, including tuition, accommodation, books and other university-related expenses. The Pearson Scholarship addresses several of these costs through its four-year financial support package.

Beyond financial assistance, the scholarship offers successful students the opportunity to study at the University of Toronto and become part of an internationally diverse academic community.

The programme’s global reach is also reflected in the university’s reported representation of scholars from 188 countries.

The Importance of Starting Early

One of the most important considerations for students interested in the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship is the multi-stage application process.

Unlike scholarships where students submit a single independent application, Pearson requires applicants to coordinate several stages.

A prospective applicant should begin by determining whether their secondary school can nominate a student.

The applicant should then discuss the opportunity with the appropriate school official, prepare for the University of Toronto admission process, identify suitable undergraduate programmes and ensure that all application requirements are completed before the relevant deadlines.

Starting early can also give students more time to prepare information about their academic achievements, leadership activities, creative projects, community involvement and future aspirations.

Recommended Application Preparation Strategy

Students interested in applying for the Pearson Scholarship can take a structured approach.

Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility

First, determine whether you meet the international student, secondary-school and university-entry requirements.

Make sure you will be starting your undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027.

Step 2: Speak to Your School

Contact your guidance counsellor, principal or head of school.

Ask whether the school is eligible to nominate a student for the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship.

If the school has not participated previously, encourage the relevant school official to review the requirements for joining the programme.

Step 3: Build Your Academic Profile

Review your academic record and identify your strongest achievements.

Keep evidence of major academic awards, competitions, research activities, projects and other accomplishments that demonstrate excellence.

Step 4: Document Your Leadership and Community Activities

Prepare a clear record of leadership positions, volunteer activities, school initiatives, community projects, extracurricular activities and other contributions.

Rather than simply listing activities, applicants should understand the impact they made through those experiences.

Step 5: Prepare Your University Application

Research the University of Toronto’s undergraduate programmes and determine which programmes align with your academic interests and career goals.

Remember that applicants can apply to up to three areas on their admission application, while the scholarship, if awarded, will be associated with the applicant’s top programme choice at the relevant decision stage.

Step 6: Submit the Admission Application

The University of Toronto admission application must be submitted by the relevant deadline of October 16, 2026 for students seeking consideration for the Pearson Scholarship.

Step 7: Complete the Pearson Scholarship Application

After school nomination and submission of the university admission application, the nominee will receive a private link to the Pearson Scholarship application.

Complete the application carefully and submit all required documentation by November 6, 2026.

Important Fraud Warning for Applicants

Prospective Pearson Scholars should be extremely cautious about individuals or organizations claiming that they can secure a scholarship, guarantee acceptance, or provide an official University of Toronto scholarship nomination in exchange for money.

The University of Toronto has specifically warned applicants about fraudulent emails and organizations claiming to assist students with Lester B. Pearson Scholarship applications.

The university states that the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship programme does not work with agencies or educational agents to recruit students or offer scholarships.

Applicants should therefore be cautious if someone

  • Promises guaranteed scholarship selection;
  • Offers a scholarship acceptance for a fee;
  • Claims to be an official Pearson Scholarship agent;
  • Requests money to secure a nomination;
  • Provides suspicious acceptance letters; or
  • Requests payment to submit an application on the student’s behalf.

Pearson Scholarship recipients can only be nominated by their current secondary school through the university’s official online process.

Students should rely on official University of Toronto information and avoid paying unaffiliated third parties for scholarship assistance.

What Happens After Selection?

Successful students become Pearson Scholars and join a global community of exceptional students at the University of Toronto.

The Pearson Program Office, housed within the University’s Centre for International Experience, provides enrichment and support opportunities for Pearson Scholars during their studies.

This can provide scholars with opportunities to engage beyond their academic programmes and participate in activities designed to enrich their international university experience.

Financial Support at a Glance

The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship provides the following:

  • Four years of undergraduate scholarship support.
  • Tuition coverage.
  • Book support.
  • Coverage of incidental fees.
  • Full residence support.
  • Study at the University of Toronto.
  • Membership in an international community of Pearson Scholars.

The university reports that approximately 37 scholars are selected annually, demonstrating the highly selective nature of the programme.

Visit HERE for more information about the University of Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship fully funded?

The scholarship covers tuition, books, incidental fees, and full residence support for four years. It is therefore a comprehensive scholarship for the eligible costs specified by the University of Toronto.

Can international students apply?

Yes. The scholarship is specifically intended for international students who are non-Canadian students requiring a study permit.

Can I apply directly without a school nomination?

No. Students must be nominated by their current secondary school. Each high school can nominate only one student per year.

Can university students apply?

The scholarship is intended for students entering first-entry undergraduate studies. Students who are already attending post-secondary studies are not eligible.

Can someone starting university in January 2027 apply?

No. Students beginning post-secondary studies in January 2027 at the University of Toronto or another post-secondary institution are not eligible for the Pearson Scholarship.

When must I begin studying at the University of Toronto?

Successful applicants must begin their undergraduate studies in September 2027.

How many students receive the scholarship?

Approximately 37 students are named Pearson Scholars each year.

Can applicants apply to more than one University of Toronto programme?

Applicants may apply to up to three areas on their University of Toronto admission application. However, the Pearson Scholarship, if awarded, will be restricted to the applicant’s top programme choice at the time of scholarship decisions.

When is the final scholarship deadline?

The final deadline for completing the Pearson Scholarship application and submitting all required documentation is November 6, 2026.

Important Deadlines Summary

Application Stage Deadline
Participating schools access nomination form July 6, 2026
High school nomination deadline October 9, 2026
New schools join the programme October 9, 2026 by noon EST
University of Toronto admission application October 16, 2026
Pearson Scholarship application and documentation November 6, 2026
Undergraduate studies begin September 2027

How to Apply

Prospective applicants should begin by speaking with their current secondary school about the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship nomination process.

They should then apply for an eligible undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto before the October 16, 2026, admission deadline.

Once nominated by their school and after submitting the university admission application, students will receive the private link required to complete the Pearson Scholarship application.

All required scholarship documentation must be submitted by November 6, 2026.

Applicants should use the University of Toronto’s official scholarship and admissions information when preparing their applications and should be particularly cautious of third parties claiming to represent the Pearson Scholarship programme.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The University of Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship 2027 is a highly competitive opportunity for exceptional international students seeking to begin an undergraduate degree in Canada.

With approximately 37 scholars selected annually, the programme seeks students who combine outstanding academic achievement with creativity, leadership potential and a commitment to making a positive contribution to the global community.

The scholarship’s four-year financial package covering tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support makes it one of the most substantial undergraduate scholarship opportunities available to international students at the University of Toronto.

However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the unique nomination process. Students cannot apply independently without a school nomination, and each high school can nominate only one student per year. Applicants must also submit their University of Toronto admission application by October 16, 2026, followed by the Pearson Scholarship application and required documentation by November 6, 2026.

Students who believe they meet the eligibility requirements should therefore begin preparing early, speak with their school leadership or guidance counsellor, strengthen their admission application, and carefully document their academic achievements, creativity, leadership, and community impact.

For ambitious international students ready to pursue undergraduate studies in Canada, the Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship 2027 could provide a transformative pathway to a world-class University of Toronto education and membership in a truly global community of scholars.

item.content:encoded:
The 2027 Martingale Scholarships offer an exceptional opportunity for talented postgraduate students to pursue fully funded Master’s or PhD studies in mathematical sciences and artificial intelligence at leading research universities in the United Kingdom. The programme is designed by the Martingale Foundation to support talented individuals from low-socioeconomic backgrounds who have the academic potential, motivation and ambition to thrive in postgraduate research. Beyond financial support, Martingale Scholars become part of a community of researchers and future leaders and receive professional development, university application guidance and access to academic and industry networks. For students who have the academic ability to pursue postgraduate research but face financial or socioeconomic barriers, the 2027 Martingale Scholarship could provide a pathway to study at some of the UK’s leading research institutions without having to carry the full financial burden of postgraduate education.

2027 Martingale Scholarships at a Glance

  • Scholarship: 2027 Martingale Scholarship
  • Study level: Master’s and PhD
  • Study location: United Kingdom
  • Entry year: 2027
  • Eligible subject areas: Mathematical Sciences and Artificial Intelligence
  • Funding: Fully funded
  • Application opening date: 12 August 2026
  • Final application deadline: 18 October 2026 at 23:59
  • Universities: Selected leading UK research universities
  • Application: Online through the Martingale Foundation

About the Martingale Foundation

The Martingale Foundation was established around the belief that family income should not prevent talented students from pursuing academic excellence and world-leading postgraduate research.

Postgraduate education can involve substantial tuition fees, living costs and research expenses. For students who do not have sufficient financial resources or family support, these costs can become a significant barrier to continuing their education.

Martingale seeks to address this challenge by combining financial support with academic, professional and personal development.

The organisation’s scholarship model therefore goes beyond simply paying university fees. Successful scholars receive funding alongside structured support intended to help them develop as researchers and future leaders.

For the 2027 intake, the Foundation is offering scholarships for selected postgraduate programmes in mathematical sciences and artificial intelligence.

What Does the 2027 Martingale Scholarship Cover?

One of the major attractions of the programme is its comprehensive approach to postgraduate support.

1. Fully Funded Master’s or PhD Study

Successful candidates receive a fully funded scholarship to pursue an eligible Master’s or PhD programme at one of Martingale’s partner universities.

This means that scholars can undertake postgraduate study while receiving financial support designed to remove major barriers associated with the cost of postgraduate education.

2. Tuition Fees and Research Expenses

The scholarship covers tuition fees and research expenses associated with the funded programme.

In addition to these costs, scholars receive a tax-free stipend set according to the Living Wage Foundation, providing financial assistance towards living costs during their studies.

This combination of academic and living-cost support is particularly important for students who may otherwise struggle to finance postgraduate education.

3. University Application Support

Applying to competitive UK universities can be complicated, particularly when candidates are applying to multiple institutions with different admissions systems and deadlines.

Martingale provides tailored support throughout the university application process.

For successful Martingale Qualified Candidates, this can include:

  • Online application workshops
  • One-to-one guidance
  • Application support
  • Application proofreading
  • Information about eligible courses
  • Deadline reminders
  • Support understanding university admissions processes

Candidates ultimately submit separate applications to the relevant partner universities, following each university’s own admissions requirements and deadlines. Martingale provides support during this stage.

4. Professional Development and Leadership Training

The scholarship also includes a substantial professional development component.

The Masters Development Programme runs alongside the Master’s degree and focuses on skills such as communication, public speaking, confidence and academic networking. Scholars also have opportunities to interact with leading academics, industry professionals and training providers.

The programme culminates in activities such as Solve for X, where participants work collaboratively on industry-related challenges and apply their academic knowledge to practical problems.

For PhD scholars, the PhD Leadership Programme provides multi-year career development and leadership training. It is intended to help scholars develop the skills, confidence and experience needed to pursue careers in academia, industry, teaching or other fields.

5. Access to a Research and Leadership Community

Martingale Scholars become members of a wider research community.

This network provides opportunities to meet other postgraduate researchers, academics, professionals and leaders across different areas of STEM.

For PhD candidates in particular, the programme provides opportunities to interact with other scholars throughout their doctoral journey, even when they are studying at different universities.

This community aspect can be valuable for building long-term academic and professional relationships.

What Can You Study Through the 2027 Martingale Scholarships?

For courses beginning in 2027, the scholarship programme is focused on two principal subject areas:

Mathematical Sciences

The mathematical sciences pathway includes selected postgraduate programmes in mathematics and related areas at participating universities.

Applicants should carefully examine the individual course requirements because eligibility, academic prerequisites and admissions requirements vary between universities and programmes.

Martingale states that financial mathematics and statistics are not currently funded for 2027 entry. Candidates whose interests are exclusively in those areas are therefore unlikely to be eligible for funding through this year’s programme.

Artificial Intelligence

The 2027 programme also supports selected postgraduate programmes related to artificial intelligence.

The available courses are offered through participating UK research universities and applicants should review the specific course listings and university requirements before applying.

The Foundation notes that the subject areas and courses supported by the programme can change from year to year. Therefore, prospective applicants should rely on the 2027 course listings rather than assuming that a programme funded in a previous year will automatically be funded for 2027 entry.

Partner Universities

Martingale is working with leading UK research universities to provide places for the 2027 scholarship programme.

The Foundation’s partner university information includes institutions such as:

  • University of Birmingham
  • University of Bristol
  • University of Cambridge
  • University of Edinburgh
  • University of Glasgow
  • Imperial College London
  • King’s College London
  • University of Manchester
  • University of Oxford
  • Queen Mary University of London
  • University College London
  • University of Warwick
  • University of York

Not every university listed as a Martingale partner necessarily provides courses funded through the 2027 scholarship cycle. Applicants should check the specific 2027 course listings before selecting a university.

Who Is the Scholarship Designed to Support?

The Martingale Scholarship is particularly aimed at talented students from low-socioeconomic backgrounds who have the academic potential and motivation to pursue postgraduate research.

Martingale considers several factors when assessing socioeconomic background, including household income, parental occupation, school background, eligibility for Free School Meals, experience of care and refugee status.

The organisation takes an intersectional approach to socioeconomic background, recognising that financial circumstances and social barriers can interact in different ways.

Academic Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate strong academic potential.

For the 2027 scholarship cycle, candidates must have achieved, or be on track to achieve, a First or Upper-Second Class degree or equivalent in a relevant subject.

Martingale also states that, in exceptional circumstances, candidates affected by compelling extenuating circumstances may still be considered even if their attainment does not meet the usual academic threshold. Such circumstances should be explained in the application.

Financial and Educational Background Requirements

The programme has specific requirements relating to an applicant’s educational and socioeconomic background.

Applicants generally need to:

  • Have faced or be facing financial barriers.
  • Typically have a household income of £45,000 or under, although Martingale considers multiple indicators when assessing socioeconomic background.
  • Have completed their GCSEs or equivalent at a state-funded school, or have received a scholarship or bursary covering at least 90% of fees at a fee-paying school or college.
  • Meet the required UK or Ireland educational history requirements.
  • Meet the Home Fee status requirements for the relevant partner university.

These requirements are important because the programme is specifically designed to widen access to postgraduate STEM research for students who may otherwise face financial or socioeconomic barriers.

Nationality and Country Eligibility

An important point for prospective international applicants is that eligibility is not simply determined by nationality.

For the 2027 scholarship, applicants must generally qualify for Home Fee status at a Martingale partner university.

The official eligibility guidance explains that this can include British or Irish nationals, individuals with Indefinite Leave to Remain or Right of Abode, and individuals with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, subject to the relevant residence requirements.

There are also other routes to Home Fee status depending on citizenship, immigration/residency status and family circumstances. Refugees and people with humanitarian protection in the UK may also qualify in relevant circumstances.

Applicants should therefore not assume that holding a particular nationality automatically makes them eligible or ineligible. The decisive issue is whether they meet the programme’s Home Fee status and other eligibility requirements.

The Foundation’s eligibility guidance should be checked carefully before applying.

UK and Ireland Schooling Requirement

The 2027 eligibility requirements also include an educational history condition.

Applicants generally need to have attended school in the UK or Ireland for at least three years between the ages of 11 and 18, or for at least seven years between the ages of 4 and 18.

The periods do not necessarily need to be continuous.

There are specific provisions for refugees, stateless people and asylum seekers, so applicants in these circumstances should review the detailed eligibility guidance rather than relying solely on the general rule.

When Does the Application Open?

Applications for the 2027 Martingale Scholarships opened on:

12 August 2026

The Foundation encourages applicants to begin preparing early and to read the application guidance carefully before submitting their forms.

Martingale Scholarship 2027 Deadline

The final application deadline is:

18 October 2026 at 23:59 UK time.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Martingale recommends allowing sufficient time to complete the application and ensure that all required information is submitted correctly.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, although the final shortlisting decision is made after the application deadline.

2027 Martingale Scholarship Application Timeline

The programme follows several stages:

Stage 1: Apply to Martingale

Applicants complete the Martingale online application form.

The application asks candidates about areas including:

  • Educational background
  • Academic qualifications
  • Family background
  • Financial circumstances
  • Motivation for postgraduate research
  • Academic interests
  • Personal circumstances

Applicants also need to provide an academic transcript, evidence of financial need and two referees.

Stage 2: Interview

Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview.

The interviews are scheduled for November 2026 and are expected to take place across the UK.

The interview assesses areas including:

  • Academic interests
  • Technical ability
  • Academic potential
  • Motivation for postgraduate study and research
  • Potential contribution to the Martingale Scholar cohort

Stage 3: Become a Martingale Qualified Candidate

Candidates who successfully progress through the selection process may become Martingale Qualified Candidates.

This is an important stage, but becoming a Qualified Candidate does not automatically guarantee a scholarship.

Qualified Candidates receive support when applying to eligible programmes at partner universities.

Stage 4: Apply to Partner Universities

Qualified Candidates then apply directly to one or more partner universities for eligible Master’s or PhD courses.

Each university has its own admissions process and deadline, meaning applicants must carefully monitor the requirements of every university and programme they apply to.

Martingale provides application support during this stage.

Stage 5: University Offers and Funding Allocation

For Master’s candidates, successful applicants who receive offers from eligible courses submit their university and course preferences to Martingale, which then allocates funded places among successful candidates.

For PhD candidates, partner universities make offers of Martingale PhD places directly to Qualified Candidates, subject to available places and university decisions.

A university offer may be conditional, in which case the associated Martingale funding is also conditional.

Key Dates for the 2027 Scholarship

The published timeline includes:

  1. 12 August 2026: Applications open.
  2. 18 October 2026: Final application deadline at 23:59.
  3. November 2026: Interviews.
  4. December 2026: Applicants are notified of outcomes.
  5. December 2026: PhD Showcase.
  6. December 2026–January 2027: Martingale application support.
  7. January–February 2027: Applications to partner universities.
  8. March 2027: Confirmation of university offers.
  9. April 2027: Offers of Martingale-funded places.

Some university programmes may have earlier admissions deadlines, so candidates must check the individual requirements of each programme.

Important: Becoming a Qualified Candidate Does Not Guarantee Funding

Applicants should understand the distinction between becoming a Martingale Qualified Candidate and receiving a Martingale Scholarship.

Qualified Candidate status means that an applicant has successfully passed the Martingale selection stage and is eligible to be considered for funding for eligible courses.

However, the number of Qualified Candidates can be greater than the number of available scholarship places.

A candidate may therefore become Qualified but not immediately receive a scholarship. Some Qualified Candidates may be placed on a waitlist, while others may receive funding later if additional places become available.

Martingale strongly encourages Qualified Candidates to apply to multiple partner universities to increase their chances of being matched with a funded place.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Prospective applicants can take several steps to strengthen their applications.

1. Confirm Your Eligibility

Before spending significant time on the application, carefully review the official eligibility criteria, particularly the requirements concerning:

  • Academic achievement
  • Home Fee status
  • UK or Ireland schooling history
  • School funding background
  • Financial circumstances
  • Eligible postgraduate study
  • Relevant academic subject

2. Research the Available Courses

Do not apply based only on the reputation of a university.

Study the actual 2027 Martingale-funded courses and check:

  • Course content
  • Entry requirements
  • Academic prerequisites
  • Research areas
  • University application deadlines
  • Whether the programme is suitable for your career and research ambitions

3. Explain Your Research Motivation Clearly

The programme is specifically focused on postgraduate research.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain why they want to pursue advanced study, what academic areas interest them and how postgraduate research fits into their longer-term goals.

4. Prepare Financial Information Carefully

Because financial need is an important component of the programme, applicants should ensure that their financial information is accurate and complete.

Martingale uses multiple indicators to assess socioeconomic circumstances, rather than relying exclusively on household income.

5. Start Early

Although applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and final shortlisting takes place after the deadline, applicants are encouraged to begin and submit their applications as soon as they are ready.

Starting early gives applicants more time to:

  • Gather academic records
  • Contact referees
  • Prepare financial information
  • Review their personal statements
  • Research eligible courses
  • Check university requirements
  • Correct errors before submission

Why the Martingale Scholarship Is More Than Tuition Funding

A major strength of the programme is that it combines financial support with long-term development.

A traditional scholarship may primarily address tuition or living costs. Martingale’s model also seeks to develop the scholar’s academic, leadership, communication and professional capabilities.

For Master’s scholars, the Development Programme provides opportunities to build confidence, communication and networking skills while engaging with academics and industry.

For PhD scholars, the Leadership Programme continues this development over multiple years, helping participants build the skills needed to navigate careers in research, academia, industry and other sectors.

Official Application and Further Information

Applicants should use the Martingale Foundation’s official resources for the most current information, including eligibility guidance, application instructions, courses and participating universities.

  • Apply here
  • Learn more here

Conclusion

The 2027 Martingale Scholarships provide a comprehensive route into postgraduate research for talented students who may face financial and socioeconomic barriers to advanced study. The programme combines funding for tuition, research expenses and living costs with university application support, professional development, leadership training and access to a growing community of researchers and professionals. For the 2027 intake, the opportunity is focused on eligible Master’s and PhD programmes in mathematical sciences and artificial intelligence at participating UK research universities. Prospective applicants should carefully check their eligibility, investigate the available courses, prepare their academic and financial information and begin their applications well before the 18 October 2026 at 23:59 deadline.

Because eligibility involves more than nationality alone, applicants should pay particular attention to the requirements surrounding Home Fee status, UK or Ireland schooling history, academic attainment and socioeconomic circumstances. Checking the official eligibility guidance is essential before submitting an application.

For eligible students with the ambition to pursue advanced research in mathematics or artificial intelligence, the Martingale Scholarship represents not only financial assistance for postgraduate study, but also an opportunity to join a structured community designed to help emerging researchers develop academically, professionally and as future leaders.
